newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FOMC meeting keeps Bund vol on its toes.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FOMC meeting keeps Bund vol on its toes.

text.p: Bund option volatility on LIFFE was supported by uncertainty about Tuesday's key Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, traders said on Monday.

With much of Europe, including Germany and France closed for a public holiday, trade was lacklustre. The U.S. FOMC, the policy making arm of the Federal Reserve meets on Tuesday, and some analysts expect interest rates to be raised.
"There's some downward pressure on the Bund futures, but with the FOMC tomorrow, volatility is steady," said a broker at a U.S. bank in London.
Traders said Bund volatility appeared expensive, and was being held in check until the FOMC meeting was out of the way.
June volatility was "all over the place", but around 6.4 percent by 1115 GMT as it expires in two days time. July and August serial options were at 5.53 percent, up from 5.37 percent at the open.
September options on the September Bund futures were at a volatility of 5.5 percent, up from 5.48 percent on the open.
September Bund options were down two basis points at 100.84 by 1045 GMT, while June was down five basis points at 101.82.

"If the FOMC does nothing, then volatility will stay supported around here," said a trader at a French house here. "But a rise in rates will push volatility off to 5.2 percent, where buying interest will be strong."
Analysts said opinion is divided about the need for a U.S. rate rise, as recent economic indicators were mixed.
"It depends how preemptive the Fed wants to be," said a U.S. bank trader.

Activity was largely confined to closing out positions in the June series ahead of June options expiry in two days time. Strikes around 101.00 to 102.50 were most active. A major U.S. brokerage was a keen seller of the 101.00 puts.
September 102.50 and 103.00 calls saw some limited trade.
